html:
The Isla refinery on Curacao was opened by Royal Dutch Shell in 1918 to refine oil from the new fields of Lake Maracaibo in Venezuela. Venezuela's shallow lake bar kept big tankers out, so the crude was shipped to Curacao.

The refinery became one of the largest in the world. It brought workers from across the Caribbean, from Suriname to Madeira, and made Curacao rich. Aruba gained its own giant refinery, Lago, in the 1920s.

The refineries supplied Allied fuel in World War II, and German submarines shelled Aruba in 1942. Shell sold the plant to the island in 1985, and it was leased to Venezuela's state oil firm until 2019. Labour unrest at the refinery helped spark the uprising of 1969.
